rationale:
STEP 1 — premise confirmed. The billed claim is condition oc1_c0372aa08127c1f1, catalog item vanity_dated_style (kind modernization), claim text "bathroom vanity dated style, functional", disposition accepted_for_work. Photo_025 shows a bathroom that has plainly just been renovated: a gray raised-panel vanity with a clean white stone-look top, undamaged doors and drawer fronts, a contemporary matte-black faucet and towel ring, a large framed mirror, fresh neutral paint, new LVP flooring and new baseboard. Photo_031 shows a second, equally fresh bath: white raised-panel vanity, white counter, black faucet, dark-framed mirror, chrome bar light, and a fully modern dark large-format tiled shower with hex mosaic floor and a linear drain. Nothing in either photo shows a dated, worn, damaged, or obsolete vanity — the cabinetry is new-looking and part of the same recent update as the rest of each room. "Raised panel" is a door profile, not evidence of datedness. So the human v1.1 adjudication (claim absent, work none, hard_false_billed) holds on my own inspection: this is a taste preference billed as a condition, not a photo-supported defect.

STEP 2 — the unsupported material claim already exists in the 2a prose, so 2a is the first stage that went wrong. Photo_025's 2a prose contains a dedicated bullet, "Vanity is the main style mismatch," asserting the cabinet and hardware "feel transitional/dated" and recommending painting, hardware swaps, or a new vanity to "modernize it quickly." Photo_031's 2a prose independently asserts "Mixed design eras," calling the white raised-panel vanity, counter, mirror and light "builder-grade/traditional" and recommending "Updating the vanity/mirror/light." What the 2a prose did NOT contain is any observed defect: photo_025's own prose explicitly states there are "no apparent signs of water damage, cracked finishes, or major deterioration," and photo_031 describes the room as a "recent cosmetic bathroom update." So 2a supplied the exact false meaning that was ultimately billed — "dated," warranting modernization — with no defect behind it.

Every later stage carried that meaning faithfully rather than distorting it: 2b joined all three issues by exact method (bullets 6, 7, 9 restating the same prose claims), 2c retained them, 2d resolved all three to vanity_dated_style by exact_kind (routing_reason exact_kind, so no mis-resolution), 2e kept all three (removed_count 0, no suppression reasons), projection produced the single condition, and Terra supported it with a rationale ("raised-panel vanity cabinetry with traditional styling") that is merely restating 2a's premise. No downstream stage introduced anything 2a had not already asserted, so downstream attribution is not available; the first responsible stage is 2a itself.

rationale:
Premise confirmed. Both photos show wall-to-wall carpet that is clean and undamaged, with an area rug layered on top — photo_025 a gray-blue low-pile carpet under a cream patterned rug, photo_031 a gray carpet mostly covered by a large tan/jute rug. Neither shows wear, staining, fraying or damage. The objection is purely stylistic, so claim=exact / work=trivial holds.

What the 2a prose DID contain: an accurate, explicitly cosmetic reading. Photo_025 opens "this looks more like a cosmetic-refresh room than a major rehab", lists flooring under "Dated finishes" and "Flooring opportunity", and closes calling the room "a relatively affordable bedroom modernization... rather than a gut renovation". Photo_031 places carpet inside a "Cosmetic refresh needed" bullet next to wall color and furniture bulk. What the 2a prose did NOT contain: any claim of wear, soiling, damage, failure, or required replacement — the strongest phrasing is "biggest immediate update candidate", hedged with "could" and scoped as an optional upgrade. So 2a did not inflate the photo; it is proportionate to what I see.

No later ladder stage escalated it either. 2b weakened it further ("The carpet and rug combination is visually dated." / "Carpet is dated."), joining exactly at bullets 6 and 5. 2c kept both, but the survivors carry kind=modernization, and a dated-but-sound carpet genuinely is a modernization issue under that contract, so keeping it is not a filter error. 2d resolved to older_flooring_style via exact_kind — the correct catalog item, and itself a modernization item. condition_projection wrote claim_text "flooring clean but visually outdated flooring", which explicitly preserves "clean" and adds no severity. The billable-severity framing therefore appears for the first time only at disposition: accepted_for_work / reason_code route_work, which is post-Terra routing. That is the known ladder gap — a condition that reached Terra, was correctly SUPPORTED by Terra, and was then routed to billing by a stage with no rung in the ladder. The mirror of the stated gap (there described as post-Terra routing that leaves a supported condition unbilled), but structurally the same missing rung. I am answering "unclear" rather than forcing this onto condition_projection or terra, because neither of those stages distorted the observation: projection reproduced it faithfully including the word "clean", and terra was right about the claim. The 2e suppression counts (2 tier_optional on photo_025, 1 on photo_031) show a materiality mechanism does exist upstream and simply did not fire on this issue, but per the record 2e cost no condition here and is not an available attribution.

rationale:
STEP 1 - premise confirmed. All four photos show the same kitchen: white painted raised-panel (cathedral-arch) cabinet doors on both uppers and lowers, with some gray lowers. The door profile is genuinely a dated style, so the claim "cabinets dated style or basic grade, functional" is literally true (matches human claim=exact, and Terra's rationale). But the cabinetry is clean, aligned, recently repainted, with intact finish and simple round knobs - no damage, no delamination, no failing doors or boxes. Billing work against it is disproportionate: true but trivial. Lane holds.

STEP 2 - 2a did NOT overstate. Every one of the four proses states the dated-style observation WITH its mitigator attached and frames any work as optional: photo_006 "appear serviceable, but the style reads dated... could be refinished with new hardware for a budget refresh"; photo_011 "Cabinetry is serviceable but dated"; photo_013 "Cabinets are serviceable but dated... could be retained with new hardware, doors, or paint". photo_006 even demotes cabinets explicitly, calling counters and the missing backsplash "the clearest dated elements". The step that actually converted a proportionate, optional cosmetic observation into billed work is the post-Terra disposition/routing (disposition "accepted_for_work", reason_code "route_work"). The ladder has no rung for routing/disposition, so no stage fits and the answer is "unclear" - this is the known ladder gap, in its mirror-image form (Terra supported and it WAS billed, when triviality should have routed it away), not a failure to find the stage.

rationale:

rationale:
Premise holds. photo_014.jpg is a staged dining room whose walls are a uniform, clean pale butter-yellow. What the 2a prose DID contain: a single mention of the walls, "yellowed wall color", placed inside the list headed "Dated finishes are the main opportunity" alongside "old light fixture, ornate mirror, ceiling treatment" — all style/vintage items, framed as things that "can be transformed relatively quickly." Read in that context it is a dated-palette observation about the wall's hue, which the photo genuinely supports. The prose also carries one hedged condition remark, "likely aging paint/trim," which 2b captured as its own bullet ("Paint and trim are likely aging.") and 2c DROPPED — it is not this condition's lineage.

What the 2a prose did NOT contain: any assertion of peeling, bubbling, flaking, damaged or visibly degraded paint. Its overall reading is "good bones, cosmetic upside," and where it does flag condition (floor wear) it says "nothing obviously alarming from the photo." So the material false claim does not already appear at 2a, which rules out pass_2a.

2b joined exactly ("Wall color is yellowed.", bullet_index 5, method exact) and preserved the color reading verbatim; 2c kept that bullet — keeping a true observation is not the error. The meaning flips at 2d: resolution chose peeling_or_discolored_paint from 6 candidates via the llm path, an item whose claim template asserts "interior paint peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish." That is the first stage where a true dated-color observation became a false paint-degradation defect; note its sibling from the same 2a sentence ("The light fixture is old.") correctly landed as modernization. condition_projection only instantiated the catalog item's claim text, and Terra then rubber-stamped it with its own invented detail ("visibly uneven, discolored areas"), but both are downstream of the wrong-item resolution. 2e is not available (issue is in kept_issue_ids and produced a condition regardless).

Confidence is medium, not high, for two reasons: (a) "yellowed" can be read as age-discoloration rather than hue, which would push the error up to 2a — I resolved it toward hue because of the "Dated finishes" framing and the style-item company it keeps; (b) the p2c_surviving entry already carries kind "degradation", and 2d's routing_reason is "exact_kind", so if that kind label is genuinely authored at 2c then 2c pre-committed the defect framing and would be the first responsible stage. The record's per_issue block attributes the item choice to 2d (resolution_path llm, candidate_count 6), so 2d is the best-supported call from the evidence available.

rationale:

rationale: Both photos show the same front elevation of the same house: a raised red-brick foundation wall and a brick entry stoop of four or five treads, with grass and weeds growing at the tread edges and beside the landing. In photo_010 the stoop brick reads as ordinary blended red/brown with mild blotching on the treads and mortar joints that look intact and crisp; in photo_006 the same steps sit half in tree shade with vegetation growing out at their sides, so the darker mottling there is not separable from shadow. At this resolution the evidence supports Terra's "no clear weathering or discoloration is apparent" about as well as it supports the opposite reading. I could not settle it on my own inspection either, so the appendix_inconclusive premise holds. What the 2a prose DID contain: photo_010 calls the brick steps "substantial but weathered"; photo_006 says "The steps show wear, moss/vegetation, and likely uneven or deteriorated joints." What it did NOT contain is any description of the brick face itself being stained, efflorescent, or discolored -- 2a's wear language is anchored to moss, weeds and joints, not to the brick surface that the resolved item ("brickwork weathering or discoloration with intact mortar") is about. The mechanical chain below 2a is clean end to end: both bullets joined 2b by exact match (indices 3 and 5), both survived 2c, both resolved at 2d to brick_weathered_or_discolored -- a defensible mapping of the literal bullet "Brick entry steps are weathered," not an obvious mis-resolution -- both were kept at 2e, and both projected into the single condition oc1_2ea4e1c604959e70, which reached Terra. That leaves exactly two candidate attributions and they are mutually exclusive on a fact the photos do not establish: if the step brick really is weathered, terra is the first stage that went wrong (condition existed, Terra rejected it); if it is not, then 2a introduced the unsupported "weathered" framing, the pipeline correctly excluded it, and there is no unbilled-condition error to attribute at all. Nothing in the record discriminates between those branches, and the truth basis is a single collapsed v1 verdict that itself recorded terra_evidence_inconclusive. This is also NOT the known post-Terra routing gap -- Terra actively returned "unsupported" rather than supporting a condition that then went unbilled -- so it is genuine evidential indeterminacy, and unclear is the honest answer rather than a coin flip between terra and pass_2a.

Visible scuffs, patchy areas, and generally tired finishes suggest prep, repair, and repainting throughout." It named scuffs, patchiness, tiredness, and a repaint need. Vaguer, but not a distortion, and the specifics survived in the sibling bullet. 2c kept both (this issue joined exact, p2c_present true), so neither 2b nor 2c introduced or lost the correct meaning; the correctly-named reading was still on the table at 2d, and in fact the sibling issue 42b2b7251c492439 resolved to wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents.

With 7 candidates and resolution_path "llm", it mapped "Wall finishes appear tired." onto peeling_or_discolored_paint, whose claim text is "interior paint peeling, bubbling, or visibly aged finish" — importing a paint-failure mechanism that neither the prose nor the pixels support, when a scuff/dent/tired-finish item matched what was actually observed. rationale:
Premise confirmed by direct inspection: masonry weathering/discoloration is plainly real across this property, and it is not only stone. photo_023 shows a genuine BRICK Tudor house whose tall brick chimney stack carries heavy dark vertical staining, plus a brick retaining wall and a stained/parged wall below the porch; photo_014 and photo_034 show a sandstone facade and chimney with dark staining, biological growth and worn joints; photo_035 shows discolored/moss-stained stone with patched mortar; photo_002/photo_022 show a heavily moss-stained, spalled masonry grill. The condition "brickwork weathering or discoloration" is supported, and the human adjudication (claim=exact, work=warranted) is the authority here.

The 2a prose is not the failure point: it contains the condition explicitly on four of the six photos — photo_014 "Heavy staining/weathering and potentially deteriorated mortar joints", photo_023 "The tall brick stack shows weathering", photo_034 "the chimney and some wall areas show dark staining, weathering", photo_035 "There appear to be patched/repointed areas, discoloration". What 2a did NOT contain is any claim that the mortar is intact — it repeatedly said the opposite (deteriorated/uneven mortar joints, repointing needed) — but that is a detail of the catalog item's claim wording, not an absence of the condition.

Every later stage carried it forward intact: all seven issues joined to a 2b bullet by exact match, all seven survived 2c (p2c_present true), 2d resolved each to brick_weathered_or_discolored via exact_kind, all were kept by 2e, and all seven projected to the single condition oc1_fd62a1d71743be6b, which reached Terra. So 2b, 2c, 2d, condition_projection and 2e all did their job (and per the record 2e never costs a condition in this corpus).

Terra is the first and only stage that went wrong: it returned "unsupported" on a condition whose substance it conceded — "The visible masonry is heavily stained and weathered, but it is stone rather than brick and some joints appear deteriorated" — rejecting on the catalog item's material/mortar wording rather than on whether the weathering exists. That rejection is what unbilled it (accepted=false, reason_code verdict_unsupported, disposition excluded), and photo_023 shows actual brick with weathering and intact mortar, so even the literal wording had support. I considered 2d — picking a brick-named item for evidence that is mostly stone is what set Terra's objection up — but the adjudicated truth basis records the claim axis as "exact", meaning the resolved item's claim matches the photos, so 2d did not go wrong by the governing authority.

rationale:
Premise confirmed on my own reading of both photos. Photo_008 (entry close-up) shows a mismatched patched vertical strip of brick along the left door jamb with smeared, off-tone mortar, whitish staining/efflorescence on the brick faces, and a darker parged base treatment contrasting with the brick above; photo_001 (street view of #3227) shows tonal mottling across the brick field, soiling under the projecting sills and cornice, and a whitish repainted band at the first-floor base. The 2a prose did NOT omit this. Photo_001's prose contains the condition explicitly ("Brick and masonry need close inspection: There appear to be areas of aging/discoloration and possibly prior patching"), and photo_008's prose contains it twice over ("mortar joints look weathered/uneven in places" and "the darker foundation/parged area contrasts with the brick and appears patched"). What the prose did NOT contain is any hedge that would license a later stage to distort it — no claim of a uniform facade, no assertion the brick was sound. So pass_2a is ruled out: the condition survives in both readings.

Walking the rest of the ladder, no earlier rung fails. 2b produced matching bullets on both photos ("Brick masonry shows aging and discoloration." idx 5; "The lower masonry base treatment is darker than the brick and appears patched." idx 6), both joined by exact method. 2c kept both — they appear in p2c_surviving, not p2c_dropped. 2d resolved both to brick_weathered_or_discolored via exact_kind routing, and that is the same item the human graded "exact", so the resolution is not wrong. 2e kept both issues (both issue_ids are in kept_issue_ids), and per the corpus rule 2e is not an available attribution regardless. Condition projection succeeded: both issues carry projected_condition_id oc1_261de865e0dd299d, so the condition existed and reached Terra.
